claims.excerpt: Under Title IV’s Acid Rain Program, sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides from the power sector were regulated through different mechanisms.
claims.claim: Title IV’s Acid Rain Program regulated power-sector sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides through different mechanisms.
claims.label: F0 faithful
claims.evidence: EPA’s Acid Rain Program addresses sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides from the power sector under Title IV. The sulfur dioxide mechanism applies an aggregate cap and allows trading; one allowance covers one ton. Its phase I began in 1995 with 263 initial units at 110 plants; substitution or compensating units brought the phase I total to 445 units. Phase II began in 2000. The final 2010 cap was 8.95 million tons. The nitrogen oxides component was rate-based for certain coal-fired units, began in 1996 and did not introduce a cap or allowance trading.
claims.narrative: The Acid Rain Program addressed sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides from the power sector, but it did not use one shared emissions mechanism.
claims.explanation: The source identifies the pollutants, sector, and Title IV, and specifies distinct sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides mechanisms.
claims.materiality: Accurately states the policy scope and central distinction.
